message.reasoning:
I am playing Monopoly as player p4.

I have $689 cash and am on CHANCE. My holdings include MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, NEW_YORK_AVENUE, PARK_PLACE, and the yellow monopoly (VENTNOR_AVENUE, MARVIN_GARDENS, ATLANTIC_AVENUE) with one house on Ventnor and Marvin. Several properties are mortgaged.

Opponent p2 has $262 and owns several properties but no complete monopolies. Opponent p3 is in jail with $3508 and a dangerous light blue hotel monopoly. I can only build on ATLANTIC_AVENUE because building must be even.

I am calculating how much cash and mortgage value I need to survive p3's light blue hotel rent. Oriental and Vermont charge $550 each, while Connecticut charges $600. I am weighing the mortgage values of my unmortgaged properties against the half-price sale value of any houses I might sell.

I am verifying my cash balance. The game state shows $689, but a step-by-step tally of prior transactions suggests $639. I need to resolve this discrepancy before making decisions.

The $689 cash balance is authoritative. Hotel cover without selling houses totals $994, which easily exceeds the $550–$600 light blue rent. Building one house on ATLANTIC_AVENUE for $150 would leave $539 cash and still clear the rent. I will build on ATLANTIC_AVENUE to maintain even building.

Standard Monopoly rent for one house on the yellow properties is $110 for Atlantic Avenue and $120 for Ventnor and Marvin Gardens. This matches the $120 rent p2 just paid me. I am now considering whether to build additional houses.

I am weighing whether to layer additional houses now. p3 is extremely wealthy and may prefer staying in jail to avoid my yellows and dark blue properties.

Unmortgaging Boardwalk would cost $220 and leave me with zero houses on dark blue, which is too weak to justify the expense. Unmortgaging the orange properties would cost $198 for a full orange monopoly, but orange houses are more expensive than yellow ones.

I cannot build three houses on the yellow monopoly. That would cost $1050, but I only have $689.

Building two houses on each property would cost $600 and leave me with $89 cash. Hotel cover after that would be $394, which is below the $550–$600 light blue rent. This path is too risky.

Selling all six houses would raise $450, giving me enough cash to survive a hotel hit without selling houses. I am reconsidering whether to sell houses now to protect against p3's light blue hotels. I also notice I just passed GO and landed on the second CHANCE space.

I rolled a 10 from Park Place to land on the light-blue Chance space. I am now directly beside p3's hotel properties: Oriental is behind me and Vermont is one space ahead.

I am mapping the post-turn roll from this Chance space. A roll of 3 lands on Connecticut, which charges a $600 hotel rent. A roll of 8 hits Pennsylvania Railroad, costing $200. All other outcomes are either safe or harmless.

The $600 Connecticut hotel is a rare but catastrophic risk. A roll of 3 has only a 2/36 chance, yet it would wipe out my cash if I build on Atlantic Avenue first. I can afford the full $600 hit outright with my current balance, so I will not spend money on houses that could force me to mortgage properties.

Building one house on Atlantic Avenue would leave only $89 cash, which is too little to pay a $600 hotel hit. I am now questioning whether paying in cash is the right standard, since selling houses afterward would cost half their value and create a net loss. I am also checking if any opponent can land on Atlantic before my next roll.

p2 cannot reach any yellow property in one roll. From Marvin Gardens, the nearest yellow spaces are 37 and 39 spaces away, which exceeds a 12-point move. The only possible landing is Mediterranean Avenue on a 12, but that would cost only $20.

p3 cannot reach my yellows in one roll from jail. Even rolling doubles would only move 12 spaces, which is still too far. No opponent can land on Atlantic, Ventnor, or Marvin before my next turn. Building houses now would generate no rent collection, so the only benefit is the improved hotel cover.

Building is strictly negative expected value right now. It costs $150 with no rent collected before the danger roll, and it drops cash below the $600 survival line.

Unmortgaging properties is also unwise. The cost of unmortgaging St James Avenue alone is $99, but its rent would only be about $14 or $28, so that money is wasted before a $600 risk.

I will not trade with p3 because they already have hotels and $3508. p2 has incomplete sets, but I should avoid giving them anything that helps them.

I checked p2's holdings for anything useful. Nothing completes my monopolies. I own all yellows and oranges, and Boardwalk is already unmortgaged. p2 has no complete sets, utilities, or jail cards that would help me. Selling p2 something would break my monopolies. Mediterranean is useless because p3 owns Baltic.

I have decided to end my turn. I will keep all cash and houses intact to survive the Connecticut hotel risk.

I am checking whether the CHANCE card has already been resolved. The public timeline only shows the $200 rent collected from p2, so the chance event may not appear in the last 20 entries.
